design_condition: The building occupies the eastern edge of the site to create a connected outdoor space beside the existing residences, while a separated access wall and compact circulation routes organize relations between neighbours, school users, and deliveries.

positive.statement: The compact footprint combines ecological measures with play, learning, and nature-experience requirements.

position.target: compact footprint and ecological play landscape
position.rationale: Compact three-wing massing visibly leaves connected exterior pockets around the building.

positive.statement: Access routes are well separated for neighbourhood and school users.

position.target: separated neighbourhood and school access routes
position.rationale: Access separation is anchored to the western and southern perimeter approaches.

positive.statement: The facility is well connected to the existing school buildings.

position.rationale: Existing buildings are not sampled; the western edge is the constrained connection location.

positive.statement: The transparent center creates attractive visual connections between the dining area and outdoor spaces.

position.rationale: The central link is clearly visible between the three wings and adjacent exterior spaces.

positive.statement: The internal access areas are based on a high spatial standard.

position.rationale: Circulation is approximated along the central connecting floor zone.

positive.statement: The structural design allows flexibility for later changes along the facade.

position.rationale: Regular eastern facade edges provide the clearest visible anchor for later facade changes.

positive.statement: The building achieves pleasant indoor climate and atmospheric quality through its architectural formulation.

position.rationale: Atmospheric and climate performance is not directly visible, so the marker covers the whole low-rise envelope.

positive.statement: The project has great spatial qualities and an attractive outdoor space.

position.target: spatial qualities and attractive outdoor space
position.rationale: Visible wing recesses create a connected outdoor region beside the compact building.

negative.statement: The exact positioning creates uncertainty because it follows neither the existing school alignment nor the adjacent streets.

position.rationale: The building’s eastern-biased footprint is directly visible; surrounding alignments are not sampled.

negative.statement: The entrance pre-zones are too exposed and should be more clearly separated from the surroundings.

position.rationale: Entrance zones are approximated along the exposed western-southern perimeter.

negative.statement: Some access areas are too small, and natural lighting in the central ground-floor zones is insufficient.

position.target: small access areas and central ground-floor lighting
position.rationale: The central ground-floor connector is visible, while access dimensions remain approximate.

negative.statement: Autonomous access to the gymnasium outside school hours can only be ensured with great effort.

position.rationale: Gymnasium is not distinguishable; an eastern wing ground-level zone provides a constrained anchor.

negative.statement: It remains questionable whether the proposed architectural solutions meet functional, technical, and economic requirements.

position.rationale: Broad functional and technical uncertainty is distributed across the sampled building envelope.

negative.statement: The project has comparatively high costs, although the target construction costs are met.

position.rationale: Cost performance has no useful spatial referent in the sampled geometry.

negative.statement: The parking facility puts strain on the root area of existing trees.

position.target: parking facility and existing tree roots
position.rationale: Parking and tree roots are absent; the eastern site edge is a directional constrained approximation.
